posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
Hummingbird:

Also, can powers on ongoing cards can be used on the turn they come into play? I used to play Magic and am used to the summoning sickness mechanic.Thanks.

Even in Magic, summoning sickness only applies to creatures, and the only hero cards in SOTM which resemble creatures are Unity's robots (though, to be clear, they function normally on the turn they're played).  Think of an Ongoing such as Ra's Blazing Tornado as like a global enchantment, or an Aura played on Ra himself, whichever makes it easier for you; regardless, if you put Firebreathing on a creature, you can pay R to give that creature +1/+0 right away, and Powers are likewise usable the turn they're played.

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
Spiff:
That is correct, since Micro-targeting Computer is destroyed, it will no longer give the +2.
Are we sure about that?  When the Explosive Wagon destroys itself, the official ruling is that it still gets its damage bonus even though it's destroyed.  Why is this different?

Wagon has an effect that triggers on its own destruction. The card needs to stay in play as that effect resolves (cards in the trash can't resolve effects obviously. That is the entire basis of the End of Days/BeeBot ruling after all). 

Micro has no such triggered effect. Also, barrage deals damage equal to the number of cards destroyed, so that presumes the card is destroyed and gone before the damage portion gets a chance to resolve.

Yeah, that's what I was getting at.  Why else wouldn't they just be called Robots?

There are perfectly legitimate reasons to call those things golems outside of the fact that Unity is at least culturally Jewish.

Yes Golems are derived from Jewish folklore, but the connotations associated with words like Robot, Android, Mech, Golem, ect, are very different. Android for instance draws images of having biological and mechanical functions and closely resembling human physiology. Robots are your run of the mill A.I. controled pieces of metal. Mechs conjure images of a Robot with a pilot. Golems on the other hand are anthropomorphic beings, which has a slight distinction from Androids who are still mostly AI based. They have real human emotion and thoughts that are not coming from mechanical proccesses like electric currents and circuits, but imbued from some outside source.

Unity's bots all have distinct personalities imbued in them, at least that is the sense that I get. So Jewish or not, Golem is the most appropriate and accurate term for the things she creates.
